    \paragraph{\(2 \Rightarrow 1\).} Suppose that Statement~2 holds, fix \(\*x \in \operatorname{supp}\left(\mu\right)\), and set \(\varepsilon := 1 - t\). Applying \eqref{eq:tilted-pinning-log-hessian} with \(\boldsymbol{\theta} = \varepsilon \*1\) shows that
    \[
    \nabla^2 \log h_{\*x}\left(\varepsilon \*1\right) \preceq \*O, \quad \forall \varepsilon \in \left(0, 1\right).
    \]
    Letting \(\varepsilon \to 0^+\) gives
    \[
    \nabla^2 \log h_{\*x}\left(\*0\right) = \frac{\left(a\left(\*x + \*e_i + \*e_j\right)\right)_{i, j \in \left[d\right]}}{a\left(\*x\right)} - \frac{\left(a\left(\*x + \*e_i\right) a\left(\*x + \*e_j\right)\right)_{i, j \in \left[d\right]}}{a\left(\*x\right)^2} \preceq \*O.
    \]
    Equivalently,
    \[
    \left(1 - \frac{a\left(\*x\right) a\left(\*x + \*e_i + \*e_j\right)}{a\left(\*x + \*e_i\right) a\left(\*x + \*e_j\right)}\right)_{i, j \in \+I_{\*x}} \succeq \*O,
    \]
    where \(\+I_{\*x} := \left\{i \in \left[d\right] \,:\, \*x + \*e_i \in \operatorname{supp}\left(\mu\right)\right\}\) denotes the set of active coordinates at \(\*x\). This is precisely the ULC condition in \eqref{eq:ulc-condition} with \(\delta = 1\).

    \paragraph{\(3 \Leftrightarrow 4\).} If \(\*x \notin \operatorname{supp}\left(\mu\right)\), downward closure implies that \(\partial^{\*x} g_{\mu}\) is identically zero. If \(\*x \in \operatorname{supp}\left(\mu\right)\), then \eqref{eq:tilted-pinning-log-hessian} and the positive definiteness of \(\operatorname{diag}\left(\boldsymbol{\theta}\right)\) show that \(h_{\*x} = \partial^{\*x} g_{\mu}\) is log-concave on \(\mathbb R_{> 0}^d\) if and only if
    \[
    \!{cov}\left(\mu^{\*x, \boldsymbol{\theta}}\right) \preceq \operatorname{diag}\left(\!{mean}\left(\mu^{\*x, \boldsymbol{\theta}}\right)\right), \quad \forall \boldsymbol{\theta} \in \mathbb R_{> 0}^d.
    \]
    This is exactly the equivalence of items~3 and~4.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- theorem-19: body_md -->
Suppose that \(\mu \in \-{WLSI}\left(1\right)\), and let \(\*Z \sim \pi_{\*m} := \bigotimes_{i = 1}^d \-{Pois}\left(m_i\right)\). Then, for every \(\boldsymbol{\lambda} \in \mathbb R^d\),
    \[
    \*E\left[e^{\left\langle\boldsymbol{\lambda},\,\*X\right\rangle}\right] \le \exp\left(\sum_{i = 1}^d m_i \left(e^{\lambda_i} - 1\right)\right) = \*E\left[e^{\left\langle\boldsymbol{\lambda},\,\*Z\right\rangle}\right].
    \]
    \label{thm:poisson-laplace-transform-domination}
<!-- end theorem-19 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
For \(N \in \mathbb N_{> 0}\), set \(X_i^{\left(N\right)} := \min\left\{X_i, N\right\}\), \(\*m^{\left(N\right)} := \*E\left[\*X^{\left(N\right)}\right]\), and
    \[
    M_N\left(\boldsymbol{\lambda}\right) := \*E\left[e^{\left\langle\boldsymbol{\lambda},\,\*X^{\left(N\right)}\right\rangle}\right], \qquad \chi_N\left(\boldsymbol{\lambda}\right) := \log M_N\left(\boldsymbol{\lambda}\right).
    \]
    Define
    \[
    f_{N, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}\left(\*n\right) := \exp\left(\sum_{i = 1}^d \lambda_i \min\left\{n_i, N\right\}\right).
    \]
    Both \(f_{N, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}\) and \(\log f_{N, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}\) are bounded, as are their forward differences. Moreover, detailed balance and finite first moments give \(\*E_{\mu}\left[\sum_{i = 1}^d b_i\right] = \sum_{i = 1}^d m_i < \infty\). Thus both functions have finite energy, and hence \(f_{N, \boldsymbol{\lambda}} \in \+A\). If \(n_i < N\), then
    \[
    \Psi\left(f_{N, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}\left(\*n\right), \nabla_i^+ f_{N, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}\left(\*n\right)\right) = f_{N, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}\left(\*n\right) \left(\lambda_i e^{\lambda_i} - e^{\lambda_i} + 1\right),
    \]
    whereas the increment vanishes when \(n_i \ge N\). Detailed balance gives
    \[
    \begin{aligned}
        \*E_{\mu}\left[\sum_{i = 1}^d b_i \Psi\left(f_{N, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}, \nabla_i^+ f_{N, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}\right)\right] &= \*E\left[\sum_{i = 1}^d b_i\left(\*X\right) \left(\lambda_i e^{\lambda_i} - e^{\lambda_i} + 1\right) f_{N, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}\left(\*X\right) \*1_{\left\{X_i < N\right\}}\right] \\
        &= \*E\left[\sum_{i = 1}^d \left(\lambda_i e^{\lambda_i} - e^{\lambda_i} + 1\right) X_i f_{N, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}\left(\*X - \*e_i\right) \*1_{\left\{X_i \le N\right\}}\right] \\
        &= \*E\left[\sum_{i = 1}^d \left(\lambda_i - 1 + e^{-\lambda_i}\right) X_i f_{N, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}\left(\*X\right) \*1_{\left\{X_i \le N\right\}}\right] \\
        &\le \*E\left[\sum_{i = 1}^d \left(\lambda_i - 1 + e^{-\lambda_i}\right) X_i^{\left(N\right)} f_{N, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}\left(\*X\right)\right].
    \end{aligned}
    \]
    Here, the last inequality uses \(\lambda_i - 1 + e^{-\lambda_i} \ge 0\). Moreover,
    \[
    \*{Ent}_{\mu}\left[f_{N, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}\right] = \left\langle\boldsymbol{\lambda},\,\*E\left[\*X^{\left(N\right)} f_{N, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}\left(\*X\right)\right]\right\rangle - M_N\left(\boldsymbol{\lambda}\right) \chi_N\left(\boldsymbol{\lambda}\right), \qquad \*E\left[X_i^{\left(N\right)} f_{N, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}\left(\*X\right)\right] = \partial_i M_N\left(\boldsymbol{\lambda}\right).
    \]
    Hence, substituting \(f_{N, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}\) into \eqref{eq:weighted-wu-log-sobolev} and dividing by \(M_N\left(\boldsymbol{\lambda}\right)\) yields
    \[
    \left\langle\boldsymbol{\lambda},\,\nabla \chi_N\left(\boldsymbol{\lambda}\right)\right\rangle - \chi_N\left(\boldsymbol{\lambda}\right) \le \sum_{i = 1}^d \left(\lambda_i - 1 + e^{-\lambda_i}\right) \partial_i \chi_N\left(\boldsymbol{\lambda}\right).
    \]
    Equivalently,
    \begin{equation}
        \sum_{i = 1}^d \left(1 - e^{-\lambda_i}\right) \partial_i \chi_N\left(\boldsymbol{\lambda}\right) \le \chi_N\left(\boldsymbol{\lambda}\right).
        \label{eq:poisson-laplace-differential-inequality}
    \end{equation}

    Fix \(\boldsymbol{\lambda} \in \mathbb R^d\). For \(s \le 0\), define the coordinatewise path from \(\*0\) to \(\boldsymbol{\lambda}\) by
    \[
    \lambda_i\left(s\right) := \log\left(1 + e^s \left(e^{\lambda_i} - 1\right)\right).
    \]
    Then \(\lambda_i\left(0\right) = \lambda_i\), \(\lambda_i\left(s\right) \to 0\) as \(s \to -\infty\), and \(\partial_s \lambda_i\left(s\right) = 1 - e^{-\lambda_i\left(s\right)}\). Hence \eqref{eq:poisson-laplace-differential-inequality} implies
    \[
    \partial_s \left(e^{-s} \chi_N\left(\boldsymbol{\lambda}\left(s\right)\right)\right) \le 0.
    \]
    Moreover, differentiability of \(\chi_N\) at \(\*0\) gives
    \[
    \lim_{s \to -\infty} e^{-s} \chi_N\left(\boldsymbol{\lambda}\left(s\right)\right) = \sum_{i = 1}^d \partial_i \chi_N\left(\*0\right) \left(e^{\lambda_i} - 1\right) = \sum_{i = 1}^d m_i^{\left(N\right)} \left(e^{\lambda_i} - 1\right).
    \]
    Monotonicity along this path therefore yields
    \[
    \chi_N\left(\boldsymbol{\lambda}\right) \le \sum_{i = 1}^d m_i^{\left(N\right)} \left(e^{\lambda_i} - 1\right).
    \]
    Finally, \(\*X^{\left(N\right)} \to \*X\) pointwise and \(\*m^{\left(N\right)} \to \*m\). Fatou's lemma gives
    \[
    \*E\left[e^{\left\langle\boldsymbol{\lambda},\,\*X\right\rangle}\right] \le \liminf_{N \to \infty} \exp\left(\chi_N\left(\boldsymbol{\lambda}\right)\right) \le \exp\left(\sum_{i = 1}^d m_i \left(e^{\lambda_i} - 1\right)\right) = \*E\left[e^{\left\langle\boldsymbol{\lambda},\,\*Z\right\rangle}\right],
    \]
    proving the claim.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- theorem-20: body_md -->
Suppose that \(\mu \in \-{WLSI}\left(1\right)\) and \(\*m := \!{mean}\left(\mu\right) \in \mathbb R_{> 0}^d\). For \(\*t \in \mathbb R^d\) satisfying \(t_i > -m_i\) for every \(i \in \left[d\right]\), define the orthant event
    \[
    \+O_{\*t} := \bigcap_{\substack{i \in \left[d\right] \\ t_i > 0}} \left\{X_i - m_i \ge t_i\right\} \cap \bigcap_{\substack{i \in \left[d\right] \\ t_i < 0}} \left\{X_i - m_i \le t_i\right\}.
    \]
    Then
    \[
    \*{Pr}_{\mu}\left[\+O_{\*t}\right] \le \exp\left(-\sum_{i = 1}^d \frac{t_i^2}{2 m_i} h\left(\frac{t_i}{m_i}\right)\right).
    \]
    \label{thm:poisson-orthant-concentration}
<!-- end theorem-20 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
\Cref{thm:poisson-laplace-transform-domination} gives the following bound on the centered log moment-generating function:
    \begin{equation}
        \log \*E\left[e^{\left\langle\boldsymbol{\lambda},\,\*X - \*m\right\rangle}\right] \le \sum_{i = 1}^d m_i \left(e^{\lambda_i} - \lambda_i - 1\right) = \log \*E\left[e^{\left\langle\boldsymbol{\lambda},\,\*Z - \*m\right\rangle}\right].
        \label{eq:centered-log-mgf-bound}
    \end{equation}
    Set
    \[
    \lambda_i := \log\left(1 + \frac{t_i}{m_i}\right).
    \]
    Each \(\lambda_i\) has the same sign as \(t_i\). Consequently, on \(\+O_{\*t}\),
    \[
    \left\langle\boldsymbol{\lambda},\,\*X - \*m\right\rangle \ge \left\langle\boldsymbol{\lambda},\,\*t\right\rangle.
    \]
    Markov's inequality and \eqref{eq:centered-log-mgf-bound} therefore give
    \[
    \begin{aligned}
        \*{Pr}_{\mu}\left[\+O_{\*t}\right] &\le \exp\left(-\left\langle\boldsymbol{\lambda},\,\*t\right\rangle\right) \*E\left[e^{\left\langle\boldsymbol{\lambda},\,\*X - \*m\right\rangle}\right] \\
        &\le \exp\left(-\sum_{i = 1}^d \left[\left(m_i + t_i\right) \log\left(1 + \frac{t_i}{m_i}\right) - t_i\right]\right) \\
        &= \exp\left(-\sum_{i = 1}^d \frac{t_i^2}{2 m_i} h\left(\frac{t_i}{m_i}\right)\right).
    \end{aligned}
    \]
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- theorem-21: body_md -->
Suppose that \(\mu \in \-{WLSI}\left(1\right)\) has mean \(\*m \in \mathbb R_{> 0}^d\), and let \(\pi_{\*m} := \bigotimes_{i = 1}^d \-{Pois}\left(m_i\right)\). Then
    \begin{equation}
        H\left(\pi_{\*m}\right) - H\left(\mu\right) \ge \-{KL}\left(\mu \| \pi_{\*m}\right) \ge 0.
        \label{eq:poisson-maximum-entropy-stability}
    \end{equation}
    Consequently, \(\pi_{\*m}\) is the unique maximizer of Shannon entropy among all measures in \(\-{WLSI}\left(1\right)\) with mean \(\*m\).
    \label{thm:poisson-maximum-entropy}
<!-- end theorem-21 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
Let \(\*Z \sim \pi_{\*m}\). Applying \Cref{thm:poisson-laplace-transform-domination} with \(\boldsymbol{\lambda} = -s \*e_i\) gives
    \begin{equation}
        \*E\left[e^{-s X_i}\right] \le \*E\left[e^{-s Z_i}\right], \quad \forall s \ge 0, \, i \in \left[d\right].
        \label{eq:poisson-coordinate-laplace-order}
    \end{equation}
    For every \(n \in \mathbb N\), Frullani's integral identity gives
    \begin{equation}
        \log n! = \int_0^{+\infty} \frac{e^{-s}}{s} \left(n - \frac{1 - e^{-s n}}{1 - e^{-s}}\right) \,\-d s.
        \label{eq:frullani-log-factorial}
    \end{equation}
    \Cref{thm:poisson-laplace-transform-domination} implies that \(\*X\) has finite exponential moments. Consequently, \(H\left(\mu\right) < \infty\) and \(\*E\left[\log X_i!\right] < \infty\) for every \(i \in \left[d\right]\); the analogous quantities for \(\*Z\) are finite as well. Taking expectations in \eqref{eq:frullani-log-factorial}, using Tonelli's theorem, and subtracting the resulting identities for \(X_i\) and \(Z_i\), whose means both equal \(m_i\), gives
    \begin{equation}
        \*E\left[\log Z_i!\right] - \*E\left[\log X_i!\right] = \int_0^{+\infty} \frac{e^{-s}}{s \left(1 - e^{-s}\right)} \left(\*E\left[e^{-s Z_i}\right] - \*E\left[e^{-s X_i}\right]\right) \,\-d s \ge 0,
        \label{eq:factorial-moment-comparison}
    \end{equation}
    where the inequality follows from \eqref{eq:poisson-coordinate-laplace-order}.

    The product Poisson mass function is
    \[
    \pi_{\*m}\left(\*n\right) = e^{-\sum_{i = 1}^d m_i} \prod_{i = 1}^d \frac{m_i^{n_i}}{n_i!}, \quad \*n \in \mathbb N^d.
    \]
    Since \(\!{mean}\left(\mu\right) = \*m\), a direct computation gives
    \[
    \-{KL}\left(\mu \| \pi_{\*m}\right) = -H\left(\mu\right) + \sum_{i = 1}^d \left(m_i - m_i \log m_i\right) + \sum_{i = 1}^d \*E\left[\log X_i!\right],
    \]
    whereas
    \[
    H\left(\pi_{\*m}\right) = \sum_{i = 1}^d \left(m_i - m_i \log m_i\right) + \sum_{i = 1}^d \*E\left[\log Z_i!\right].
    \]
    Subtracting these identities and applying \eqref{eq:factorial-moment-comparison} gives
    \[
    H\left(\pi_{\*m}\right) - H\left(\mu\right) = \-{KL}\left(\mu \| \pi_{\*m}\right) + \sum_{i = 1}^d \left(\*E\left[\log Z_i!\right] - \*E\left[\log X_i!\right]\right) \ge \-{KL}\left(\mu \| \pi_{\*m}\right).
    \]
    This proves \eqref{eq:poisson-maximum-entropy-stability}. The product Poisson law is ULC and therefore belongs to \(\-{WLSI}\left(1\right)\) by \Cref{thm:ulc-modified-log-sobolev-inequality}. Finally, if \(H\left(\mu\right) = H\left(\pi_{\*m}\right)\), then \eqref{eq:poisson-maximum-entropy-stability} forces \(\-{KL}\left(\mu \| \pi_{\*m}\right) = 0\), and hence \(\mu = \pi_{\*m}\), proving uniqueness.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- definition-11: body_md -->
An integral polymatroid rank function on \(\left[d\right]\) is a map \(r:2^{\left[d\right]} \to \mathbb N\) satisfying the following properties:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item Normalization: \(r\left(\varnothing\right) = 0\).
        \item Monotonicity: \(r\left(S\right) \le r\left(T\right)\) whenever \(S \subseteq T \subseteq \left[d\right]\).
        \item Submodularity: \(r\left(S\right) + r\left(T\right) \ge r\left(S \cup T\right) + r\left(S \cap T\right)\) for all \(S, T \subseteq \left[d\right]\).
    \end{itemize}
    For \(\*n \in \mathbb N^d\) and \(S \subseteq \left[d\right]\), write \(\*n\left(S\right) := \sum_{i \in S} n_i\). The discrete polymatroid associated with \(r\) is the set of independent vectors
    \[
    P_r := \left\{\*n \in \mathbb N^d \,:\, \forall S \subseteq \left[d\right], \, \*n\left(S\right) \le r\left(S\right)\right\}.
    \]
<!-- end definition-11 -->
<!-- theorem-22: body_md -->
For every integral polymatroid rank function \(r\) and every activity vector \(\boldsymbol{\lambda} \in \mathbb R_{> 0}^d\), the measure \(\mu_{r, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}\) is ULC.
    \label{thm:polymatroid-independent-vectors-ulc}
<!-- end theorem-22 -->
<!-- remark-13: body_md -->
Lorentzian polynomials provide an alternative proof of \Cref{thm:polymatroid-independent-vectors-ulc}; see \cite{BH20}. Indeed, it suffices to observe that \(P_r\) is \(M^{\natural}\)-convex and then apply a suitable homogenization.
<!-- end remark-13 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
Write \(\mu := \mu_{r, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}\) and \(a\left(\*n\right) := \*n! \mu\left(\*n\right)\). Then
    \[
    a\left(\*n\right) \propto \boldsymbol{\lambda}^{\*n}, \quad \*n \in P_r.
    \]
    Fix \(\*n \in P_r\), and let \(\+I_{\*n} := \left\{k \in \left[d\right] \,:\, \*n + \*e_k \in P_r\right\}\) be its set of active coordinates. For every \(i, j \in \+I_{\*n}\),
    \[
    \frac{a\left(\*n\right) a\left(\*n + \*e_i + \*e_j\right)}{a\left(\*n + \*e_i\right) a\left(\*n + \*e_j\right)} = \*1_{\left\{\*n + \*e_i + \*e_j \in P_r\right\}}.
    \]
    Consequently, for \(\delta = 1\), the matrix on the left-hand side of \eqref{eq:ulc-condition} reduces to
    \[
    \*M_{\*n} := \left(\*1_{\left\{\*n + \*e_i + \*e_j \notin P_r\right\}}\right)_{i, j \in \+I_{\*n}}.
    \]
    It remains to show that \(\*M_{\*n}\) is positive semidefinite.

    For \(S \subseteq \left[d\right]\), define the slack
    \[
    s_{\*n}\left(S\right) := r\left(S\right) - \*n\left(S\right).
    \]
    Since \(r\) is submodular and \(\*n\left(\cdot\right)\) is modular, \(s_{\*n}\) is a nonnegative, integer-valued submodular function. Moreover,
    \[
    i \in \+I_{\*n} \iff \*n + \*e_i \in P_r \iff s_{\*n}\left(S\right) \ge 1 \text{ for every } S \subseteq \left[d\right] \text{ containing } i,
    \]
    while, for \(i, j \in \+I_{\*n}\),
    \[
    \left(\*M_{\*n}\right)_{ij} = 1 \iff \*n + \*e_i + \*e_j \notin P_r \iff s_{\*n}\left(S\right) = 1 \text{ for some } S \subseteq \left[d\right] \text{ containing } i, j.
    \]

    Let \(B_{\*n} := \left\{i \in \+I_{\*n} \,:\, \left(\*M_{\*n}\right)_{ii} = 1\right\}\), and define a relation on \(B_{\*n}\) by setting \(i \sim j\) whenever \(\left(\*M_{\*n}\right)_{ij} = 1\). This relation is reflexive and symmetric. To prove transitivity, suppose that \(i \sim j\) and \(j \sim k\). Choose \(S, T \subseteq \left[d\right]\) such that \(i, j \in S\), \(j, k \in T\), and \(s_{\*n}\left(S\right) = s_{\*n}\left(T\right) = 1\). Since \(j\) is active and belongs to \(S \cap T\), while \(i\) is active and belongs to \(S \cup T\), the preceding characterization, together with the submodularity of \(s_{\*n}\), gives
    \[
    2 = s_{\*n}\left(S\right) + s_{\*n}\left(T\right) \ge s_{\*n}\left(S \cap T\right) + s_{\*n}\left(S \cup T\right) \ge 2.
    \]
    Both terms on the right are at least \(1\), so equality holds throughout and \(s_{\*n}\left(S \cup T\right) = 1\). Therefore, \(i \sim k\), and \(\sim\) is an equivalence relation on \(B_{\*n}\). Moreover, for any \(i \in \+I_{\*n} \setminus B_{\*n}\), \(\*n + 2 \*e_i \in P_r\), so \(s_{\*n}\left(S\right) \ge 2\) for every \(S \subseteq \left[d\right]\) containing \(i\). Thus \(\left(\*M_{\*n}\right)_{ij} = \left(\*M_{\*n}\right)_{ji} = 0\) for every \(j \in \+I_{\*n}\).

    Therefore, after reordering the coordinates, \(\*M_{\*n}\) is block diagonal: each equivalence class of \(\sim\) contributes an all-ones block, while the coordinates outside \(B_{\*n}\) contribute a zero block. Every such block is positive semidefinite, so \(\*M_{\*n} \succeq \*O\). Since this holds for every \(\*n \in P_r\), the measure \(\mu_{r, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}\) is ULC.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- corollary-5: body_md -->
The probability-generating function of \(\mu_{r, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}\) is completely log-concave.
<!-- end corollary-5 -->
<!-- corollary-6: body_md -->
Set \(R := r\left(\left[d\right]\right)\), \(\Lambda := \sum_{i = 1}^d \lambda_i\), \(C := R + \Lambda\). Define a Markov kernel \(Q\) on \(P_r\) by
    \[
    Q\left(\*n, \*n - \*e_i\right) := \frac{n_i}{C}, \quad i \in \left[d\right], \, n_i > 0, \qquad Q\left(\*n, \*n + \*e_i\right) := \frac{\lambda_i}{C}, \quad i \in \+I_{\*n},
    \]
    with the remaining probability assigned to staying at \(\*n\), where \(\+I_{\*n} := \left\{i \in \left[d\right] \,:\, \*n + \*e_i \in P_r\right\}\). Then \(Q\) is reversible with respect to \(\mu_{r, \boldsymbol{\lambda}}\), and its lazification \(\bar Q := \left(I + Q\right) / 2\) satisfies a modified log-Sobolev inequality with constant at least \(1 / \left(2 C\right)\). Consequently, for every \(\varepsilon \in \left(0, 1 / 2\right)\),
    \[
    T_{\-{mix}}\left(\varepsilon; \bar Q\right) = O_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}}\left(\left(d + R\right) \left(\log R + \log \log\left(d + R\right) + \log \frac{1}{\varepsilon}\right)\right).
    \]
    Moreover, this chain can be implemented directly given a membership oracle for \(P_r\).
    \label{cor:polymatroid-birth-death-mixing}
<!-- end corollary-6 -->
<!-- theorem-23: body_md -->
Let \(G\) be a graph with maximum degree at most \(\Delta\), where \(\Delta \ge 1\), and let \(\*A_G\) be its adjacency matrix. Set \(\lambda^{\star} := -\lambda_{\min}\left(\*A_G\right)\), and suppose that \(q \ge 3\), \(0 < B < 1\), and
    \[
    \lambda^{\star} \left(1 - B\right) B^{1 - \Delta} < 1.
    \]
    Then the embedded antiferromagnetic Potts measure \(\mu_{G, B}\) is \(\delta\)-ULC with
    \[
    \delta := 1 - \lambda^{\star} \left(1 - B\right) B^{1 - \Delta}.
    \]
    \label{thm:antiferromagnetic-potts-ulc}
<!-- end theorem-23 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
Set \(p := q - 1\). Fix \(\*x \in \Omega\), write \(\sigma := \varphi^{-1}\left(\*x\right)\), and let \(U := \left\{v \in V \,:\, \sigma_v = q\right\}\). The active coordinates at \(\*x\) are precisely \(U \times \left[p\right]\). If \(U = \varnothing\), the ULC condition is vacuous, so assume that \(U \ne \varnothing\). Since \(\Omega \subseteq \left\{0, 1\right\}^{V \times \left[p\right]}\), the factorial-weighted mass satisfies \(a\left(\*x\right) := \*x! \mu_{G, B}\left(\*x\right) = \mu_{G, B}\left(\*x\right)\). Let \(\*M_{\*x}\) denote the first matrix on the left-hand side of \eqref{eq:ulc-condition}. A direct computation gives
    \[
    \left(\*M_{\*x}\right)_{\left(v, k\right), \left(w, \ell\right)} = \begin{cases}
        1, & v = w, \\
        1 - B^2, & v \ne w, \, vw \in E, \, k = \ell, \\
        1 - B, & v \ne w, \, vw \in E, \, k \ne \ell, \\
        0, & v \ne w, \, vw \notin E.
    \end{cases}
    \]
    Let \(\*A_U\) be the adjacency matrix of the induced subgraph \(G\left[U\right]\), let \(\*I_U\) be the identity matrix indexed by \(U\), and let \(\*J_p\) and \(\*I_p\) be the \(p \times p\) all-ones and identity matrices, respectively. Grouping the active coordinates by vertex gives
    \[
    \*M_{\*x} = \*I_U \otimes \*J_p + \left(1 - B\right) \*A_U \otimes \left(\*J_p + B \*I_p\right).
    \]
    Diagonalizing the matrices acting on the color coordinates yields
    \[
    \lambda_{\min}\left(\*M_{\*x}\right) = B \left(1 - B\right) \lambda_{\min}\left(\*A_U\right) + \min\left\{0, \, p \left(1 + \left(1 - B\right) \lambda_{\min}\left(\*A_U\right)\right)\right\}.
    \]
    By eigenvalue interlacing, \(\lambda_{\min}\left(\*A_U\right) \ge \lambda_{\min}\left(\*A_G\right) = -\lambda^{\star}\). Moreover, since \(B^{1 - \Delta} \ge 1\), the hypothesis also implies \(\lambda^{\star} \left(1 - B\right) < 1\). Hence,
    \[
    \lambda_{\min}\left(\*M_{\*x}\right) \ge -B \left(1 - B\right) \lambda^{\star} + \min\left\{0, \, p \left(1 - \left(1 - B\right) \lambda^{\star}\right)\right\} = -B \left(1 - B\right) \lambda^{\star}.
    \]
    Let \(\*D_{\*x}\) denote the diagonal matrix in \eqref{eq:ulc-condition}. For \(c \in \left[q\right]\), let \(d_c^{\sigma}\left(v\right)\) be the number of neighbors of \(v\) having color \(c\) under \(\sigma\). Let \(\*e_{v, k}\) denote the standard basis vector corresponding to \(\left(v, k\right)\). Switching an active vertex \(v \in U\) from color \(q\) to color \(k \in \left[p\right]\) gives
    \[
    \left(\*D_{\*x}\right)_{\left(v, k\right), \left(v, k\right)} = \frac{a\left(\*x\right)}{a\left(\*x + \*e_{v, k}\right)} = B^{d_q^{\sigma}\left(v\right) - d_k^{\sigma}\left(v\right)} \ge B^{\Delta},
    \]
    where the inequality follows from \(d_q^{\sigma}\left(v\right) - d_k^{\sigma}\left(v\right) \le \deg_G\left(v\right) \le \Delta\). Thus \(\lambda_{\min}\left(\*D_{\*x}\right) \ge B^{\Delta}\), and hence
    \[
    \*M_{\*x} + \left(1 - \delta\right) \*D_{\*x} \succeq \left(-B \left(1 - B\right) \lambda^{\star} + \left(1 - \delta\right) B^{\Delta}\right) \*I_{U \times \left[p\right]} = \*O,
    \]
    where the equality follows from the definition of \(\delta\). Hence the ULC condition holds at every \(\*x \in \Omega\).
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- corollary-7: body_md -->
In the setting of \Cref{thm:antiferromagnetic-potts-ulc}, \(P_{\-{GD}}\) has spectral gap at least
    \[
    \gamma_{\-{GD}} \ge \frac{\delta B^{\Delta}}{q n}.
    \]
    \label{cor:q-potts-rapid-mixing}
<!-- end corollary-7 -->
<!-- corollary-8: body_md -->
Fix \(q \ge 3\) and \(\zeta \in \left(0, 1 / 2\right)\). Let \(G\) be a uniformly random \(\Delta\)-regular graph on \(n\) vertices, and suppose that
    \[
    1 - B \le \left(\frac{1}{2} - \zeta\right) \frac{\log \Delta}{\Delta}.
    \]
    For all sufficiently large \(\Delta\), with probability \(1 - o_n\left(1\right)\), the embedded Potts measure is \(\delta\)-ULC with \(\delta\) as in \Cref{thm:antiferromagnetic-potts-ulc} and \(\delta \ge 1 / 2\), and
    \[
    T_{\-{mix}}\left(\varepsilon; P_{\-{GD}}\right) = O_q\left(\sqrt{\Delta} n^2 \log \frac{1}{\varepsilon}\right).
    \]
    \label{cor:q-potts-random-regular-mixing}
<!-- end corollary-8 -->
<!-- theorem-24: body_md -->
If \(\mu\) is \(\kappa\)-Laguerre-ULC, then
    \[
    \kappa \, \*{Var}_{\mu}\left[f\right] \le \*E_{\mu}\left[\sum_{i = 1}^d x_i \left(\partial_i f\left(\*x\right)\right)^2\right], \quad \forall f \in \+C_{\-c}^{\infty}\left(\mathbb{R}_{> 0}^d\right).
    \]
    More generally, if the matrix \(\*K_{\*x}\) defined in \eqref{eq:laguerre-local-curvature} is positive definite for every \(\*x \in \mathbb{R}_{> 0}^d\), then
    \[
    \*{Var}_{\mu}\left[f\right] \le \*E_{\mu}\left[\left(\nabla f\right)^{\top} \*K^{-1} \nabla f\right], \quad \forall f \in \+C_{\-c}^{\infty}\left(\mathbb{R}_{> 0}^d\right),
    \]
    where \(\*K = \*K_{\*x}\) in the integrand.
    \label{thm:laguerre-functional-inequalities}
<!-- end theorem-24 -->
<!-- remark-14: body_md -->
\Cref{thm:laguerre-functional-inequalities} may also be proved by developing the integrated Bakry--\'Emery\xspace calculus directly for the Laguerre diffusion. The argument parallels the one in \Cref{sec:bakry-emery-birth-death}.
<!-- end remark-14 -->
<!-- remark-15: body_md -->
The Laguerre Brascamp--Lieb inequality can also be derived from the intertwining framework of \cite[Theorem~3.1]{ABJ18}. Indeed, for the auxiliary Langevin generator \(\+L_0 = \Delta - \nabla V \cdot \nabla\), choose the distortion matrix
    \[
    \*A\left(\*x\right) := \operatorname{diag} \left(\frac{1}{x_i}\right)_{i \in \left[d\right]}.
    \]
    Since \(\+L_0 x_i = -\partial_i V\left(\*x\right)\), the curvature matrix in that framework is
    \[
    \*A^{-1} \*M_{\*A} \*A = \nabla^2 V\left(\*x\right) - \left(\+L_0 \*A^{-1}\right)\left(\*x\right) \*A\left(\*x\right) = \nabla^2 V\left(\*x\right) + \operatorname{diag} \left(\frac{\partial_i V\left(\*x\right)}{x_i}\right)_{i \in \left[d\right]} = \*K_{\*x}.
    \]
    Consequently, \cite[Theorem~3.1]{ABJ18}, together with a cutoff approximation on the positive orthant, yields the same Brascamp--Lieb inequality.
<!-- end remark-15 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
Suppose first that \(\mu\) is \(\kappa\)-Laguerre-ULC, and fix \(0 < \kappa' < \kappa\). By the curvature limit above, there are \(\delta_N > 0\) such that \(N \delta_N \to \kappa'\) and \(\mu_N\) is \(\delta_N\)-ULC. Applying \Cref{thm:ulc-poincare-inequality} to \(f_N := f \circ \iota_N\) and multiplying the resulting inequality by \(N\) gives
    \[
    N \delta_N \, \*{Var}_{\mu_N}\left[f_N\right] \le N \+E_N\left(f_N, f_N\right).
    \]
    The Riemann-sum convergence of \(\mu_N\), together with the Dirichlet-form limit \eqref{eq:dirichlet-form-convergence}, yields
    \[
    \kappa' \, \*{Var}_{\mu}\left[f\right] \le \+E\left(f, f\right) = \*E_{\mu}\left[\sum_{i = 1}^d x_i \left(\partial_i f\left(\*x\right)\right)^2\right].
    \]
    Letting \(\kappa' \to \kappa\) proves the weighted Poincar\'e\xspace inequality.

    Now suppose that \(\*K_{\*x} \succ \*O\) for every \(\*x \in \mathbb{R}_{> 0}^d\). On compact truncations, the curvature expansion implies that \(\*K_{\*n}^{\left(N\right)} \succ \*O\) for all sufficiently large \(N\). Hence \Cref{thm:discrete-brascamp-lieb} gives
    \[
    \*{Var}_{\mu_N}\left[f_N\right] \le \*E_{\mu_N}\left[\left(\nabla^+ f_N\right)^{\top} \left(\*K^{\left(N\right)}\right)^{-1} \nabla^+ f_N\right].
    \]
    Uniformly on the support of \(f\),
    \[
    \nabla^+ f_N\left(\*n\right) = \frac{1}{N} \nabla f\left(\*x\right) + O\left(N^{-2}\right), \qquad \left(\*K_{\*n}^{\left(N\right)}\right)^{-1} = N^2 \*K_{\*x}^{-1} + O\left(N\right).
    \]
    Therefore, the integrand on the right-hand side converges to \(\left(\nabla f\right)^{\top} \*K^{-1} \nabla f\). Passing to the limit in the discrete Brascamp--Lieb inequality and then removing the compact truncation proves the claim.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- example-7: body_md -->
Fix \(\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_d, \kappa > 0\), and let
    \[
    \mu := \bigotimes_{i = 1}^d \-{Gamma}\left(\alpha_i, \kappa\right).
    \]
    A direct calculation shows that \(\mu\) is exactly \(\kappa\)-Laguerre-ULC; that is, equality holds in \eqref{eq:laguerre-ulc-condition}. Moreover, the weighted Poincar\'e\xspace inequality in \Cref{thm:laguerre-functional-inequalities} has the sharp constant \(\kappa\): for each \(i\), the function \(f_i\left(\*x\right) := x_i - \alpha_i / \kappa\) is an eigenfunction of \(-\+L\) with eigenvalue \(\kappa\).

    This example also admits a discrete approximation that preserves the curvature constant. For \(N > \kappa\), let \(X_{N, 1}, \dots, X_{N, d}\) be independent random variables with \(X_{N, i} \sim \-{NB}\left(\alpha_i, \delta_N\right)\), where \(\delta_N := \kappa / N\). Then
    \[
    \-{Law}\left(\frac{1}{N} \left(X_{N, 1}, \dots, X_{N, d}\right)\right) \Rightarrow \mu,
    \]
    while the product negative binomial law is exactly \(\delta_N\)-ULC. Its birth-death generator has spectral gap \(\delta_N\), so the generator accelerated by \(N\) has spectral gap \(N \delta_N = \kappa\), consistent with the Laguerre limit.
<!-- end example-7 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
Write
    \[
    \*m_t := \!{mean}\left(\nu_t\right), \qquad \*a_t := \*m_t - \*X_t.
    \]
    The conditional-expectation formula for the birth rates (\Cref{cor:denoising-birth-rates-conditional-expectation}) gives
    \[
    q_{t, i}\left(\*X_{t-}\right) = \frac{a_{t-, i}}{1 - t}.
    \]
    Fix the current state \(\*X_{t-} = \*x\). As long as \(\*X_t\) does not jump, differentiating the explicit posterior formula gives
    \[
    \partial_t \nu_{t, \*x}\left(\*n\right) = -\frac{\nu_{t, \*x}\left(\*n\right)}{1 - t} \sum_{i = 1}^d \left(n_i - m_{t, i}\right) = -\nu_{t, \*x}\left(\*n\right) \sum_{i = 1}^d \frac{n_i - m_{t, i}}{a_{t-, i}} q_{t, i}\left(\*X_{t-}\right).
    \]
    If \(\*X_t\) jumps from \(\*x\) to \(\*x + \*e_i\), then Bayes' rule gives
    \[
    \nu_{t, \*x + \*e_i}\left(\*n\right) = \nu_{t-, \*x}\left(\*n\right) \frac{n_i - x_i}{m_{t-, i} - x_i},
    \]
    and therefore
    \[
    \nu_{t, \*x + \*e_i}\left(\*n\right) - \nu_{t-, \*x}\left(\*n\right) = \nu_{t-, \*x}\left(\*n\right) \frac{n_i - m_{t-, i}}{a_{t-, i}}.
    \]
    Combining the continuous evolution and the jump updates yields
    \[
    \,\-d \nu_t\left(\*n\right) = \nu_{t-}\left(\*n\right) \sum_{i = 1}^d \frac{n_i - m_{t-, i}}{a_{t-, i}} \left(\-d X_{t, i} - q_{t, i}\left(\*X_{t-}\right) \,\-d t\right).
    \]
    Here and below, a summand with \(a_{t-, i} = 0\) is set equal to zero. Indeed, \(a_{t-, i} = 0\) implies that \(\nu_{t-}\) is supported on \(\left\{\*n \in \mathbb N^d \,:\, n_i = X_{t-, i}\right\}\), so the \(i\)-th birth rate and the corresponding numerator both vanish. This proves the asserted linear-tilt equation.

    Finally, for \(T < 1\),
    \[
    \int_0^T \frac{\*1_{\left\{a_{t-, i} > 0\right\}}}{a_{t-, i}} q_{t, i}\left(\*X_{t-}\right) \,\-d t = \int_0^T \frac{\*1_{\left\{a_{t-, i} > 0\right\}}}{1 - t} \,\-d t \le -\log\left(1 - T\right).
    \]
    Thus the stochastic integral defining \(Z_{t, i}\) is integrable and is a martingale on \(\left[0, T\right]\).
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
Write
    \[
    \*m_t := \!{mean}\left(\nu_t\right), \qquad \*a_t := \*m_t - \*X_t, \qquad F_t := \*E_{\nu_t}\left[f\right], \qquad G_t := \*E_{\nu_t}\left[\Phi\left(f\right)\right],
    \]
    and define
    \[
    c_{t, i} :=
    \begin{cases}
        \displaystyle \frac{\*{Cov}_{\*n \sim \nu_t}\left[f\left(\*n\right), n_i\right]}{a_{t, i}}, & a_{t, i} > 0, \\
        0, & a_{t, i} = 0.
    \end{cases}
    \]
    Both \(F_t\) and \(G_t\) are martingales, and \Cref{thm:poisson-linear-tilt} gives
    \[
    \,\-d F_t = \sum_{i = 1}^d c_{t-, i} \left(\-d X_{t, i} - q_{t, i}\left(\*X_{t-}\right) \,\-d t\right).
    \]
    When \(\*X_t\) jumps in coordinate \(i\), the corresponding jump of \(F_t\) is \(c_{t-, i}\). The jump-process It\^o\xspace formula therefore yields
    \[
    \,\-d \Phi\left(F_t\right) = \Phi'\left(F_{t-}\right) \,\-d F_t + \sum_{i = 1}^d \Psi\left(F_{t-}, c_{t-, i}\right) \,\-d X_{t, i}.
    \]
    Taking expectations and using the compensators of the coordinate birth processes gives
    \[
    \,\-d \*E\left[\Phi\left(F_t\right)\right] = \*E\left[\sum_{i = 1}^d q_{t, i}\left(\*X_t\right) \Psi\left(F_t, c_{t, i}\right)\right] \,\-d t = \frac{1}{1 - t} \*E\left[\sum_{i = 1}^d a_{t, i} \Psi\left(F_t, c_{t, i}\right)\right] \,\-d t,
    \]
    where the second equality uses the conditional-expectation formula \(q_{t, i}\left(\*X_t\right) = a_{t, i} / \left(1 - t\right)\) for the birth rates (\Cref{cor:denoising-birth-rates-conditional-expectation}). Since \(\*{Ent}_{\nu_t}^{\Phi}\left[f\right] = G_t - \Phi\left(F_t\right)\) and \(\*E\left[G_t\right]\) is constant, this proves the general \(\Phi\)-entropy identity.

    For \(\Phi\left(x\right) = x^2\), we have \(\Psi\left(u, v\right) = v^2\); substituting it gives the variance identity. For \(\Phi\left(x\right) = x \log x\), the homogeneity identity
    \[
    a \, \Psi\left(u, \frac{v}{a}\right) = u \, \Psi\left(a, \frac{v}{u}\right)
    \]
    holds for \(a, u > 0\). Applying it with \(a \gets a_{t, i}\), \(u \gets F_t\), and \(v \gets \*{Cov}_{\*n \sim \nu_t}\left[f\left(\*n\right), n_i\right]\) gives the entropy identity.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
For \(t \in \left[0, 1\right)\) and \(\*x \in \operatorname{supp}\left(\mu_t\right)\), define \(\rho_t^{\*x} := \-{Law}\left(\*X_1 - \*X_t \mid \*X_t = \*x\right)\). Then
    \[
    \rho_t^{\*x} = \left(1 - t\right) * \mu^{\*x}.
    \]
    \label{lem:tilted-pinning-conditional-law}
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
For \(t \in \left(0, 1\right)\), by the posterior formula \eqref{eq:posterior-formula}, for every \(\*k \in \mathbb N^d\) such that \(\*x + \*k \in \operatorname{supp}\left(\mu\right)\),
    \[
    \rho_t^{\*x}\left(\*k\right) = \nu_{t, \*x}\left(\*x + \*k\right) = \frac{t^{\left\|\*x\right\|_1}}{\mu_t\left(\*x\right)} \left(1 - t\right)^{\left\|\*k\right\|_1} \mu\left(\*x + \*k\right) \prod_{i = 1}^d \binom{x_i + k_i}{x_i}.
    \]
    The factor \(t^{\left\|\*x\right\|_1} / \mu_t\left(\*x\right)\) does not depend on \(\*k\). Comparing the remaining expression with \Cref{def:weighted-pinning} therefore gives \(\rho_t^{\*x} = \left(1 - t\right) * \mu^{\*x}\). The case \(t = 0\) follows directly from \(\*X_0 = \*0\).
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
Fix \(t \in \left(0, 1\right)\) and condition on \(\*X_t = \*x\). Write \(\rho := \rho_t^{\*x}\) and \(g\left(\*k\right) := f\left(\*x + \*k\right)\), and set
    \[
    \*m := \!{mean}\left(\rho\right), \qquad \*c := \*{Cov}_{\*k \sim \rho}\left[g\left(\*k\right), \*k\right], \qquad \*C := \!{cov}\left(\rho\right).
    \]
    If \(m_i = 0\), then the coordinate map \(\*k \mapsto k_i\) vanishes \(\rho\)-almost surely and hence \(c_i = 0\). We may therefore restrict to the coordinates on which \(m_i > 0\) and set \(\*z := \operatorname{diag}\left(\*m\right)^{-1} \*c\). The Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and spectral independence yield
    \[
    \left(\*z^{\top} \*c\right)^2 = \*{Cov}_{\*k \sim \rho}\left[g\left(\*k\right), \*z^{\top} \*k\right]^2 \le \*{Var}_{\rho}\left[g\right] \*z^{\top} \*C \*z.
    \]
    By \Cref{lem:tilted-pinning-conditional-law}, \(\rho = \left(1 - t\right) * \mu^{\*x}\), so the spectral independence hypothesis gives \(\*C \preceq \eta_t \operatorname{diag}\left(\*m\right)\). Hence,
    \[
    \left(\*z^{\top} \*c\right)^2 \le \eta_t \, \*{Var}_{\rho}\left[g\right] \*z^{\top} \operatorname{diag}\left(\*m\right) \*z = \eta_t \, \*{Var}_{\rho}\left[g\right] \*z^{\top} \*c.
    \]
    Dividing by \(\*z^{\top} \*c\) when it is positive, with the zero case being immediate, gives
    \[
    \sum_{i = 1}^d \frac{\*{Cov}_{\*n \sim \nu_{t, \*x}}\left[f\left(\*n\right), n_i\right]^2}{\!{mean}\left(\nu_{t, \*x}\right)_i - x_i} = \sum_{i = 1}^d \frac{c_i^2}{m_i} = \*z^{\top} \*c \le \eta_t \, \*{Var}_{\nu_{t, \*x}}\left[f\right].
    \]
    Applying the variance identity in \Cref{thm:phi-entropy-evolution} and averaging over \(\*x \sim \mu_t\) now gives
    \[
    \partial_t \*E\left[\*{Var}_{\nu_t}\left[f\right]\right] \ge -\frac{\eta_t}{1 - t} \*E\left[\*{Var}_{\nu_t}\left[f\right]\right].
    \]
    The same argument at \(t = 0\), where \(\*X_0 = \*0\) and \(\rho_0^{\*0} = \mu\), gives the asserted right-derivative inequality at the endpoint.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- theorem-25: body_md -->
Let \(\rho\) be a probability measure on \(\Omega \subseteq \mathbb R^d\), let \(\boldsymbol{\varphi}: \Omega \to \mathbb R^d\) be measurable, and define
    \[
    \chi_{\rho, \boldsymbol{\varphi}}\left(\boldsymbol{\theta}\right) := \log \*E_{\rho}\left[e^{\left\langle\boldsymbol{\theta},\,\boldsymbol{\varphi}\right\rangle}\right].
    \]
    For \(\boldsymbol{\theta}\) in the interior of the effective domain of \(\chi_{\rho, \boldsymbol{\varphi}}\), let \(\rho_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}\) be the exponential tilt
    \[
    \frac{\,\-d \rho_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}}{\,\-d \rho}\left(\*x\right) = \exp\left(\left\langle\boldsymbol{\theta},\,\boldsymbol{\varphi}\left(\*x\right)\right\rangle - \chi_{\rho, \boldsymbol{\varphi}}\left(\boldsymbol{\theta}\right)\right).
    \]
    If \(\*m = \*E_{\rho_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}}\left[\boldsymbol{\varphi}\right]\), then every \(\widetilde{\rho} \ll \rho\) satisfying \(\*E_{\widetilde{\rho}}\left[\boldsymbol{\varphi}\right] = \*m\) obeys
    \[
    \-{KL}\left(\widetilde{\rho} \| \rho\right) = \-{KL}\left(\widetilde{\rho} \| \rho_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}\right) + \-{KL}\left(\rho_{\boldsymbol{\theta}} \| \rho\right) \ge \-{KL}\left(\rho_{\boldsymbol{\theta}} \| \rho\right).
    \]
    Thus \(\rho_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}\) is the unique minimizer of relative entropy among probability measures with mean statistic \(\*m\). Means on the relative boundary of the mean domain are obtained by limits of exponential tilts.
    \label{thm:maximum-entropy-principle}
<!-- end theorem-25 -->
<!-- theorem-26: body_md -->
In the setting of \Cref{thm:maximum-entropy-principle}, the log-Laplace transform is smooth and convex on the interior of its effective domain and satisfies
    \[
    \nabla \chi_{\rho, \boldsymbol{\varphi}}\left(\boldsymbol{\theta}\right) = \*E_{\rho_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}}\left[\boldsymbol{\varphi}\right], \qquad \nabla^2 \chi_{\rho, \boldsymbol{\varphi}}\left(\boldsymbol{\theta}\right) = \*{Cov}_{\rho_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}}\left[\boldsymbol{\varphi}\right].
    \]
    If the exponential family is minimal, then \(\chi_{\rho, \boldsymbol{\varphi}}\) is strictly convex. For every mean \(\*m\) in the interior of the mean domain, let \(\boldsymbol{\theta}\left(\*m\right)\) be the unique parameter satisfying \(\nabla \chi_{\rho, \boldsymbol{\varphi}}\left(\boldsymbol{\theta}\left(\*m\right)\right) = \*m\). Let \(\chi_{\rho, \boldsymbol{\varphi}}^*\) denote the convex conjugate of \(\chi_{\rho, \boldsymbol{\varphi}}\). Then
    \[
    \chi_{\rho, \boldsymbol{\varphi}}^*\left(\*m\right) = \-{KL}\left(\rho_{\boldsymbol{\theta}\left(\*m\right)} \| \rho\right), \qquad \nabla \chi_{\rho, \boldsymbol{\varphi}}^*\left(\*m\right) = \boldsymbol{\theta}\left(\*m\right),
    \]
    and, whenever the covariance is nonsingular,
    \[
    \nabla^2 \chi_{\rho, \boldsymbol{\varphi}}^*\left(\*m\right) = \*{Cov}_{\rho_{\boldsymbol{\theta}\left(\*m\right)}}\left[\boldsymbol{\varphi}\right]^{-1}.
    \]
    In the nonminimal case, the same identities hold after restriction to the affine hull of \(\boldsymbol{\varphi}\left(\operatorname{supp}\left(\rho\right)\right)\).
    \label{thm:log-Laplace-transform}
<!-- end theorem-26 -->
<!-- remark-16: body_md -->
When \(\boldsymbol{\varphi}\left(\*x\right) = \*x\), 
    \[
    \operatorname{dom} \boldsymbol{\theta} = \operatorname{relint}\left(\operatorname{dom} \chi_{\rho, \boldsymbol{\varphi}}^*\right) \subseteq \operatorname{relint}\left(\operatorname{conv}\left(\Omega\right)\right).
    \]
    Boundary means are handled by approximation with interior means.
<!-- end remark-16 -->
<!-- definition-12: body_md -->
Let \(\rho\) be a probability measure on \(\Omega\), let \(\psi: \operatorname{conv} \Omega \times \operatorname{conv} \Omega \to \mathbb R_{\ge 0}\), and let \(\eta > 0\). We say that \(\rho\) is \(\eta\)-entropically stable with respect to \(\psi\) if
    \[
    \psi\left(\!{mean}\left(\boldsymbol{\lambda} * \rho\right), \!{mean}\left(\rho\right)\right) \le \eta \, \-{KL}\left(\boldsymbol{\lambda} * \rho \| \rho\right), \quad \forall \boldsymbol{\lambda} \in \mathbb R_{> 0}^d.
    \]
    Unless otherwise specified, we take
    \[
    \psi\left(\*x, \*y\right) := \sum_{i = 1}^d \Psi\left(y_i, x_i - y_i\right),
    \]
    where \(\Psi\left(u, v\right) := \left(u + v\right) \log\left(u + v\right) - u \log u - v \left(\log u + 1\right)\) and \(\Psi\left(0, 0\right) := 0\).
<!-- end definition-12 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
Suppose that \(\rho\) is \(\eta\)-entropically stable with respect to \(\psi\). Then every probability measure \(\widetilde{\rho} \ll \rho\) satisfies
    \[
    \psi\left(\!{mean}\left(\widetilde{\rho}\right), \!{mean}\left(\rho\right)\right) \le \eta \, \-{KL}\left(\widetilde{\rho} \| \rho\right).
    \]
    \label{lem:entropic-stability-tilted}
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
Set \(\*m_0 := \!{mean}\left(\rho\right)\) and \(\*m := \!{mean}\left(\widetilde{\rho}\right)\). We may assume that \(\-{KL}\left(\widetilde{\rho} \| \rho\right) < \infty\), since otherwise the claim is immediate. First suppose that \(\*m\) lies in the interior of the mean domain. Let \(\rho_{\boldsymbol{\theta}\left(\*m\right)}\) be the exponential tilt of \(\rho\) with mean \(\*m\). By \Cref{thm:maximum-entropy-principle} and entropic stability,
    \[
    \psi\left(\*m, \*m_0\right) \le \eta \, \-{KL}\left(\rho_{\boldsymbol{\theta}\left(\*m\right)} \| \rho\right) \le \eta \, \-{KL}\left(\widetilde{\rho} \| \rho\right).
    \]
    For a general mean, fix \(\varepsilon \in \left(0, 1\right)\) and define \(\widetilde{\rho}_{\varepsilon} := \left(1 - \varepsilon\right) \widetilde{\rho} + \varepsilon \rho\). Its mean \(\*m_{\varepsilon} = \left(1 - \varepsilon\right) \*m + \varepsilon \*m_0\) lies in the relative interior of the mean domain. Applying the preceding argument and using convexity of relative entropy gives
    \[
    \psi\left(\*m_{\varepsilon}, \*m_0\right) \le \eta \, \-{KL}\left(\widetilde{\rho}_{\varepsilon} \| \rho\right) \le \eta \left(1 - \varepsilon\right) \-{KL}\left(\widetilde{\rho} \| \rho\right).
    \]
    Letting \(\varepsilon \to 0^+\) and using lower semicontinuity of \(\psi\) proves the claim.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
Fix \(t \in \left(0, 1\right)\). Suppose that \(\rho_t^{\*x}\) is \(\eta\)-entropically stable with respect to \(\psi\) for every \(\*x \in \operatorname{supp}\left(\mu_t\right)\). Then every nonnegative \(f \in \+C_{\-c}\left(\operatorname{supp}\left(\mu\right)\right)\) satisfies
    \[
    \partial_t \*E\left[\*{Ent}_{\nu_t}\left[f\right]\right] \ge -\frac{\eta}{1 - t} \*E\left[\*{Ent}_{\nu_t}\left[f\right]\right].
    \]
    \label{lem:entropic-stability-implies-entropy-conservation}
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
Condition on \(\*X_t = \*x\), and write \(\rho := \rho_t^{\*x}\), \(g\left(\*k\right) := f\left(\*x + \*k\right)\). If \(\*E_{\rho}\left[g\right] = 0\), then \(g = 0\) \(\rho\)-almost surely, so both the conditional entropy and the corresponding term in the entropy evolution identity vanish. Suppose that \(\*E_{\rho}\left[g\right] > 0\), and define the \(g\)-tilt \(\widetilde{\rho}\) by
    \[
    \frac{\,\-d \widetilde{\rho}}{\,\-d \rho}\left(\*k\right) := \frac{g\left(\*k\right)}{\*E_{\rho}\left[g\right]}.
    \]
    Then
    \[
    \!{mean}\left(\widetilde{\rho}\right) - \!{mean}\left(\rho\right) = \frac{\*{Cov}_{\*k \sim \rho}\left[g\left(\*k\right), \*k\right]}{\*E_{\rho}\left[g\right]},
    \]
    while
    \[
    \*E_{\rho}\left[g\right] \, \-{KL}\left(\widetilde{\rho} \| \rho\right) = \*{Ent}_{\rho}\left[g\right] = \*{Ent}_{\nu_{t, \*x}}\left[f\right].
    \]
    Therefore, \Cref{lem:entropic-stability-tilted} gives
    \[
    \begin{aligned}
        \*E_{\rho}\left[g\right] \sum_{i = 1}^d \Psi\left(\!{mean}\left(\rho\right)_i, \frac{\*{Cov}_{\*k \sim \rho}\left[g\left(\*k\right), k_i\right]}{\*E_{\rho}\left[g\right]}\right) &= \*E_{\rho}\left[g\right] \, \psi\left(\!{mean}\left(\widetilde{\rho}\right), \!{mean}\left(\rho\right)\right) \\
        &\le \eta \, \*E_{\rho}\left[g\right] \, \-{KL}\left(\widetilde{\rho} \| \rho\right) \\
        &= \eta \, \*{Ent}_{\nu_{t, \*x}}\left[f\right].
    \end{aligned}
    \]
    Since \(\!{mean}\left(\rho\right)_i = \!{mean}\left(\nu_{t, \*x}\right)_i - x_i\), substituting this estimate into the entropy identity in \Cref{thm:phi-entropy-evolution} and averaging over \(\*x \sim \mu_t\) yields
    \[
    \partial_t \*E\left[\*{Ent}_{\nu_t}\left[f\right]\right] \ge -\frac{\eta}{1 - t} \*E\left[\*{Ent}_{\nu_t}\left[f\right]\right].
    \]
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
Suppose that \(\boldsymbol{\lambda} * \rho\) is \(\eta\)-spectrally independent for every \(\boldsymbol{\lambda} \in \mathbb R_{> 0}^d\). Then \(\rho\) is \(\eta\)-entropically stable with respect to \(\psi\).
    \label{lem:spectral-independence-implies-entropic-stability}
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
We may discard coordinates that vanish \(\rho\)-almost surely and work on the affine hull of \(\operatorname{supp}\left(\rho\right)\). For \(\boldsymbol{\theta} \in \mathbb R^d\), define
    \[
    \chi\left(\boldsymbol{\theta}\right) := \log \*E_{\*k \sim \rho}\left[e^{\left\langle\boldsymbol{\theta},\,\*k\right\rangle}\right], \qquad \rho_{\boldsymbol{\theta}} := e^{\boldsymbol{\theta}} * \rho,
    \]
    and write \(\*m_0 := \!{mean}\left(\rho\right)\). For \(\*m\) in the interior of the mean domain, let \(\boldsymbol{\theta}\left(\*m\right)\) be the parameter satisfying \(\!{mean}\left(\rho_{\boldsymbol{\theta}\left(\*m\right)}\right) = \*m\), and set
    \[
    H\left(\*m\right) := \-{KL}\left(\rho_{\boldsymbol{\theta}\left(\*m\right)} \| \rho\right), \qquad G\left(\*m\right) := \psi\left(\*m, \*m_0\right).
    \]
    By \Cref{thm:log-Laplace-transform},
    \[
    \nabla^2 H\left(\*m\right) = \!{cov}\left(\rho_{\boldsymbol{\theta}\left(\*m\right)}\right)^{-1}.
    \]
    On the other hand, 
    \[
    G\left(\*m\right) = \sum_{i = 1}^d \left[m_i \log\left(\frac{m_i}{m_{0, i}}\right) - m_i + m_{0, i}\right], \qquad \nabla^2 G\left(\*m\right) = \operatorname{diag}\left(\*m\right)^{-1}.
    \]
    Spectral independence of \(\rho_{\boldsymbol{\theta}\left(\*m\right)}\) gives
    \[
    \!{cov}\left(\rho_{\boldsymbol{\theta}\left(\*m\right)}\right) \preceq \eta \operatorname{diag}\left(\!{mean}\left(\rho_{\boldsymbol{\theta}\left(\*m\right)}\right)\right) = \eta \operatorname{diag}\left(\*m\right).
    \]
    Hence,
    \[
    \eta \nabla^2 H\left(\*m\right) - \nabla^2 G\left(\*m\right) \succeq \*O.
    \]
    Here and above, inverse matrices are interpreted on the affine hull; equivalently, the Hessian comparison follows from the corresponding generalized-inverse inequality on its tangent space. Thus \(\eta H - G\) is convex. Note that \(\!{mean}\left(\rho_{\boldsymbol{\theta}\left(\*m_0\right)}\right) = \*m_0 = \!{mean}\left(\rho\right)\), so \(\boldsymbol{\theta}\left(\*m_0\right) = 0\). Together with \Cref{thm:log-Laplace-transform}, we have
    \[
    H\left(\*m_0\right) = \-{KL}\left(\rho_{\boldsymbol{\theta}\left(\*m_0\right)} \| \rho\right) = 0 = G\left(\*m_0\right),
    \]
    \[
    \nabla H\left(\*m_0\right) = \boldsymbol{\theta}\left(\*m_0\right) = 0 = \nabla G\left(\*m_0\right).
    \]
    It follows that \(G\left(\*m\right) \le \eta H\left(\*m\right)\) throughout the interior of the mean domain. In particular, this holds for \(\*m = \!{mean}\left(\boldsymbol{\lambda} * \rho\right)\) for every \(\boldsymbol{\lambda} \in \mathbb R_{> 0}^d\), which is precisely \(\eta\)-entropic stability.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
Fix \(t \in \left(0, 1\right)\) and \(\*x \in \operatorname{supp}\left(\mu_t\right)\). By \Cref{lem:tilted-pinning-conditional-law},
    \[
    \rho_t^{\*x} = \left(1 - t\right) * \mu^{\*x}.
    \]
    Consequently, for every \(\boldsymbol{\lambda} \in \mathbb R_{> 0}^d\),
    \[
    \boldsymbol{\lambda} * \rho_t^{\*x} = \left(\left(1 - t\right) \boldsymbol{\lambda}\right) * \mu^{\*x}.
    \]
    Note that
    \[
    \*x \in \operatorname{supp}\left(\mu_t\right) = \left\{\*x \in \mathbb N^d \,:\, \exists \*x' \in \operatorname{supp}\left(\mu\right), \, \*x \le \*x'\right\} = \Omega.
    \]
    The hypothesis of the proposition therefore implies that every exponential tilt of \(\rho_t^{\*x}\) is \(\eta\)-spectrally independent. By \Cref{lem:spectral-independence-implies-entropic-stability}, \(\rho_t^{\*x}\) is \(\eta\)-entropically stable. Applying \Cref{lem:entropic-stability-implies-entropy-conservation} gives
    \[
    \partial_t \*E\left[\*{Ent}_{\nu_t}\left[f\right]\right] \ge -\frac{\eta}{1 - t} \*E\left[\*{Ent}_{\nu_t}\left[f\right]\right], \quad \forall t \in \left(0, 1\right).
    \]
    The same argument gives the asserted right-derivative inequality at \(t = 0\).
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- definition-13: body_md -->
Let \(\mu\) be a finitely supported probability measure on \(\mathbb N^d\), and let \(N \in \mathbb N\) satisfy
    \[
    N \ge \max_{\*n \in \operatorname{supp}\left(\mu\right)} \left\|\*n\right\|_1.
    \]
    The homogenized generating polynomial of \(\mu\) is defined by
    \[
    \+H_N g_{\mu}\left(\theta_0, \boldsymbol{\theta}\right) := \sum_{\*n \in \operatorname{supp}\left(\mu\right)} \frac{\mu\left(\*n\right)}{\left(N - \left\|\*n\right\|_1\right)!} \theta_0^{N - \left\|\*n\right\|_1} \boldsymbol{\theta}^{\*n}, \quad \left(\theta_0, \boldsymbol{\theta}\right) \in \mathbb R^{d + 1}.
    \]
    \label{def:homogenized-generating-polynomial}
<!-- end definition-13 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
Let \(\mu\) be supported on a finite downward closed subset of \(\mathbb N^d\). Then \(\mu\) is ULC if and only if, for every \(N \in \mathbb N\) satisfying \(N \ge \max_{\*n \in \operatorname{supp}\left(\mu\right)} \left\|\*n\right\|_1\), the homogenized generating polynomial \(\+H_N g_{\mu}\) is Lorentzian.
    \label{lem:ulc-homogenization-lorentzian}
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
Write \(a\left(\*n\right) := \*n! \mu\left(\*n\right)\). Suppose first that \(\mu\) is ULC. By \Cref{thm:ulc-generating-function-characterization}, \(g_{\mu}\) is strongly log-concave. Fix a nonzero derivative \(h = \partial^{\*x} g_{\mu}\). By log-concavity, pointwise on \(\mathbb R_{> 0}^d\),
    \[
    \*A := \nabla h \nabla h^{\top} - h \nabla^2 h \succeq \*O.
    \]
    In particular,
    \[
    A_{ii} = \left(\partial_i h\right)^2 - h \partial_{ii} h \ge 0, \quad \forall i \in \left[d\right].
    \]
    Since \(h\) has nonnegative coefficients, \(h, \partial_i h,\partial_{ii} h \ge 0\), and hence \(0 \le \sqrt{A_{ii}} \le \partial_i h\). Moreover, positive semidefiniteness of \(\*A\) gives
    \[
    \left|A_{ij}\right| \le \sqrt{A_{ii} A_{jj}} \le \partial_i h \, \partial_j h, \quad \forall i, j \in \left[d\right], \, i \ne j.
    \]
    Thus, for \(i \ne j\),
    \[
    \partial_i h\,\partial_j h \ge \left|A_{ij}\right| \ge -A_{ij} = h \partial_{ij} h - \partial_i h \,\partial_j h,
    \]
    and therefore \(h \partial_{ij} h \le 2 \partial_i h \, \partial_j h\). For \(i = j\), the stronger inequality
    \[
    h \partial_{ii} h \le \left(\partial_i h\right)^2
    \]
    follows directly from \(A_{ii} \ge 0\). Hence, \(g_{\mu}\) is \(2\)-Rayleigh \cite[Definition~2.18]{BH20}. Since \(\operatorname{supp}\left(\mu\right)\) is downward closed, \(g_{\mu}\left(\*0\right) = \mu\left(\*0\right) > 0\). Hence, \cite[Lemma~2.22]{BH20} implies that \(\operatorname{supp}\left(\mu\right)\) is \(M^{\natural}\)-convex. Consequently,
    \[
    \+J_N := \left\{\left(N - \left\|\*n\right\|_1, \*n\right) \,:\, \*n \in \operatorname{supp}\left(\mu\right)\right\}
    \]
    is \(M\)-convex.

    For \(\*n \in \operatorname{supp}\left(\mu\right)\) with \(\left\|\*n\right\|_1 \le N - 2\), the corresponding quadratic derivative is
    \[
    \partial_0^{N - \left\|\*n\right\|_1 - 2} \partial^{\*n} \+H_N g_{\mu}\left(\theta_0, \boldsymbol{\theta}\right) = \frac{a\left(\*n\right)}{2} \theta_0^2 + \sum_{i = 1}^d a\left(\*n + \*e_i\right) \theta_0 \theta_i + \frac{1}{2} \sum_{i, j = 1}^d a\left(\*n + \*e_i + \*e_j\right) \theta_i \theta_j.
    \]
    Its Hessian is
    \[
    \begin{pmatrix}
        a\left(\*n\right) & \left(a\left(\*n + \*e_i\right)\right)_{i \in \left[d\right]}^{\top} \\
        \left(a\left(\*n + \*e_i\right)\right)_{i \in \left[d\right]} & \left(a\left(\*n + \*e_i + \*e_j\right)\right)_{i, j \in \left[d\right]}
    \end{pmatrix}.
    \]
    Since \(a\left(\*n\right) > 0\), the Schur complement shows that this Hessian has at most one positive eigenvalue if and only if
    \[
    \left(\frac{a\left(\*n + \*e_i\right) a\left(\*n + \*e_j\right)}{a\left(\*n\right)} - a\left(\*n + \*e_i + \*e_j\right)\right)_{i, j \in \+I_{\*n}} \succeq \*O,
    \]
    where \(\+I_{\*n} := \left\{i \in \left[d\right] \,:\, \*n + \*e_i \in \operatorname{supp}\left(\mu\right)\right\}\). This follows directly from the ULC matrix condition in \eqref{eq:ulc-condition} by a congruence transformation. Hence every quadratic derivative has at most one positive eigenvalue. Together with the \(M\)-convexity of \(\+J_N\), \cite[Theorem~2.25]{BH20} implies that \(\+H_N g_{\mu}\) is Lorentzian.

    Conversely, suppose that \(\+H_N g_{\mu}\) is Lorentzian. Its quadratic derivatives have at most one positive eigenvalue, so the same Schur-complement calculation gives the ULC matrix condition at every \(\*n\) with \(\left\|\*n\right\|_1 \le N - 2\). The remaining boundary cases are automatic because no second increment lies in the support. Thus \(\mu\) is ULC.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
First suppose that \(\mu\) has finite support. For every sufficiently large \(N\), define
    \[
    F_{\mu, N}\left(\boldsymbol{\theta}\right) := N! \, \+H_N g_{\mu}\left(1, \boldsymbol{\theta} / N\right) = \sum_{\*n \in \operatorname{supp}\left(\mu\right)} \mu\left(\*n\right) \frac{N!}{\left(N - \left\|\*n\right\|_1\right)! N^{\left\|\*n\right\|_1}} \boldsymbol{\theta}^{\*n}.
    \]
    By the equivalence between Lorentzian and completely log-concave polynomials \cite[Theorem~2.30]{BH20}, \(\+H_N g_{\mu}\) is completely log-concave. Since complete log-concavity is preserved under restriction to \(\theta_0 = 1\), positive diagonal rescaling of the remaining variables, and multiplication by a positive constant, it follows that \(F_{\mu, N}\) is completely log-concave. As \(N \to \infty\), \(F_{\mu, N}\) and all their directional derivatives converge pointwise to those of \(g_{\mu}\). Log-concavity of every derivative passes to the limit, so \(g_{\mu}\) is completely log-concave.

    For general \(\mu\), let \(\mu_N\) denote its normalized restriction to \(\left\{\*n \in \mathbb N^d \,:\, \left\|\*n\right\|_1 \le N\right\}\). It is straightforward to check that \(\mu_N\) is ULC. By the preceding argument, \(g_{\mu_N}\) is completely log-concave. Note that \(g_{\mu_N}\) and all its directional derivatives converge pointwise to those of \(g_{\mu}\). Log-concavity of every derivative passes to the limit, so \(g_{\mu}\) is completely log-concave.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
For \(v \in V\) and \(c \in \left[q\right]\), define the local heat-bath probabilities by
    \[
    p_c^{\sigma}\left(v\right) := \frac{B^{d_c^{\sigma}\left(v\right)}}{\sum_{a = 1}^q B^{d_a^{\sigma}\left(v\right)}}, \quad v \in V, \, c \in \left[q\right].
    \]
    The Glauber Dirichlet form is
    \[
    \+E_{P_{\-{GD}}}\left(f, f\right) = \frac{1}{2 n} \*E_{\sigma \sim \mu_{G, B}}\left[\sum_{v \in V} \sum_{c = 1}^q p_c^{\sigma}\left(v\right) \left(f\left(\sigma^{v \gets c}\right) - f\left(\sigma\right)\right)^2\right].
    \]
    By detailed balance, the two orientations of every update between color \(q\) and a color \(c \in \left[q - 1\right]\) contribute equally. Pairing these orientations and discarding updates between two nonreference colors gives
    \[
    \+E_{P_{\-{GD}}}\left(f, f\right) \ge \frac{1}{n} \*E_{\sigma \sim \mu_{G, B}}\left[\sum_{\substack{v \in V \\ \sigma_v = q}} \sum_{c = 1}^{q - 1} p_c^{\sigma}\left(v\right) \left(f\left(\sigma^{v \gets c}\right) - f\left(\sigma\right)\right)^2\right].
    \]
    Under the downward closed embedding, \eqref{eq:birth-death-generator} gives
    \[
    \+E\left(f, f\right) = \*E_{\sigma \sim \mu_{G, B}}\left[\sum_{\substack{v \in V \\ \sigma_v = q}} \sum_{c = 1}^{q - 1} B^{d_c^{\sigma}\left(v\right) - d_q^{\sigma}\left(v\right)} \left(f\left(\sigma^{v \gets c}\right) - f\left(\sigma\right)\right)^2\right],
    \]
    where \(\+E\) is the Dirichlet form of the embedded linear-death generator. Note that
    \[
    \frac{B^{d_c^{\sigma}\left(v\right) - d_q^{\sigma}\left(v\right)}}{p_c^{\sigma}\left(v\right)} = \sum_{a = 1}^q B^{d_a^{\sigma}\left(v\right) - d_q^{\sigma}\left(v\right)} \le q B^{-\Delta},
    \]
    since \(d_a^{\sigma}\left(v\right) - d_q^{\sigma}\left(v\right) \ge -\Delta\) for every \(a \in \left[q\right]\). Hence,
    \[
    \+E_{P_{\-{GD}}}\left(f, f\right) \ge \frac{B^{\Delta}}{q n} \+E\left(f, f\right).
    \]
    Combining this comparison with \Cref{thm:ulc-poincare-inequality} proves the spectral-gap bound.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
Set \(\alpha := 1 / 2 - \zeta\). Since \(1 - B \le \alpha \log \Delta / \Delta = o_{\Delta}\left(1\right)\), for all sufficiently large \(\Delta\),
    \[
    \log \frac{1}{B} \le \frac{1 - B}{B} \le \left(\frac{1}{2} - \frac{\zeta}{2}\right) \frac{\log \Delta}{\Delta}.
    \]
    Consequently,
    \[
    B^{1 - \Delta} \le B^{-\Delta} \le \Delta^{1 / 2 - \zeta / 2}.
    \]
    On the event in the eigenvalue estimate preceding the corollary, \(\lambda^{\star} \le 3 \sqrt{\Delta}\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). Hence,
    \[
    \lambda^{\star} \left(1 - B\right) B^{1 - \Delta} \le 3 \sqrt{\Delta} \frac{\alpha \log \Delta}{\Delta} \Delta^{1 / 2 - \zeta / 2} = 3 \alpha \Delta^{-\zeta / 2} \log \Delta = o_{\Delta}\left(1\right).
    \]
    Thus, for all sufficiently large \(\Delta\), this quantity is at most \(1 / 2\) with probability \(1 - o_n\left(1\right)\). By \Cref{thm:antiferromagnetic-potts-ulc}, the embedded Potts measure is then \(\delta\)-ULC with \(\delta \ge 1 / 2\). Therefore, \Cref{cor:q-potts-rapid-mixing} implies
    \[
    \gamma_{\-{GD}}^{-1} \le \frac{q n}{\delta} B^{-\Delta} \le 2 q n \Delta^{1 / 2 - \zeta / 2}.
    \]

    Let \(\mu_{\min} := \min_{\sigma \in \left[q\right]^V} \mu_{G, B}\left(\sigma\right)\). Since \(B^{\left|E\right|} \le B^{m_G\left(\sigma\right)} \le 1\), the normalizing constant of \(\mu_{G, B}\) is at most \(q^n\), and hence
    \[
    \mu_{\min} \ge \frac{B^{\left|E\right|}}{q^n}.
    \]
    Using \(\left|E\right| = n \Delta / 2\) and the bound on \(-\log B\), we obtain
    \[
    \log \frac{1}{\mu_{\min}} \le n \log q + \frac{n \Delta}{2} \log \frac{1}{B} \le n \log q + \frac{n \Delta}{2} \left(\frac{1}{2} - \frac{\zeta}{2}\right) \frac{\log \Delta}{\Delta} = O_q\left(n \log \Delta\right).
    \]
    The kernel \(P_{\-{GD}}\) is ergodic and reversible. Moreover, it is the average of the single-site conditional-expectation operators, each of which is an orthogonal projection on \(L^2\left(\mu_{G, B}\right)\); hence \(P_{\-{GD}}\) is positive semidefinite. Applying \Cref{thm:functional-inequality-mixing} now gives
    \[
    \begin{aligned}
        T_{\-{mix}}\left(\varepsilon; P_{\-{GD}}\right) &\le \left\lceil\frac{1}{\gamma_{\-{GD}}} \left(\log \frac{1}{2 \varepsilon} + \frac{1}{2} \log \frac{1}{\mu_{\min}}\right)\right\rceil \\
        &= O_q\left(n \Delta^{1 / 2 - \zeta / 2} \left(\log \frac{1}{\varepsilon} + n \log \Delta\right)\right) \\
        &= O_q\left(\sqrt{\Delta} n^2 \log \frac{1}{\varepsilon}\right).
    \end{aligned}
    \]
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- definition-14: body_md -->
A measurable function \(r: X \times \+N\left(X\right) \to \mathbb R_{\ge 0}\) is a Papangelou intensity of \(\mathbb P\) with respect to \(\nu\) if the Georgii--Nguyen--Zessin identity
    \begin{equation}
        \*E_{\mathbb P}\left[\int_X H\left(x, \eta - \delta_x\right) \eta\left(\-d x\right)\right] = \*E_{\mathbb P}\left[\int_X H\left(x, \eta\right) r_x\left(\eta\right) \nu\left(\-d x\right)\right]
        \label{eq:papangelou-intensity}
    \end{equation}
    holds for every nonnegative measurable \(H\), where \(r_x\left(\eta\right) := r\left(x, \eta\right)\).
<!-- end definition-14 -->
<!-- theorem-27: body_md -->
Suppose that the cylinder generator in \eqref{eq:point-process-glauber-generator} is essentially self-adjoint on \(L^2\left(\mathbb P\right)\), its closure has only constants in its kernel, and \(\+K_{\eta}^{\left(\delta\right)}\left(h\right) \ge 0\) for \(\mathbb P\)-almost every \(\eta\) and every compactly supported test function \(h\). Then \(\+G\) satisfies the Poincar\'e\xspace inequality with constant \(\delta\):
    \[
    \delta \, \*{Var}_{\mathbb P}\left[F\right] \le \+E_{\+G}\left(F, F\right), \quad \forall F \in \+D\left(\+E_{\+G}\right).
    \]
    \label{thm:point-process-curvature-criterion}
<!-- end theorem-27 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
The lifted law \(\mathbb P_{\mu}\) has density
    \begin{equation}
        \frac{\,\-d \mathbb P_{\mu}}{\,\-d \Pi_{\bar\nu}}\left(\eta\right) = e \, d^{\left\|\*N\left(\eta\right)\right\|_1} a\left(\*N\left(\eta\right)\right),
        \label{eq:point-process-lift-density}
    \end{equation}
    and Papangelou intensity
    \begin{equation}
        r_{\left(x, i\right)}\left(\eta\right) = d \frac{a\left(\*n + \*e_i\right)}{a\left(\*n\right)}, \qquad \*n = \*N\left(\eta\right).
        \label{eq:point-process-lift-papangelou}
    \end{equation}
    Moreover, if \(F = f \circ \*N\), then the point-process generator \(\+G\) in \eqref{eq:point-process-glauber-generator} satisfies
    \[
    \+G F\left(\eta\right) = \sum_{i = 1}^d \frac{a\left(\*n + \*e_i\right)}{a\left(\*n\right)} \nabla_i^+ f\left(\*n\right) + \sum_{i = 1}^d n_i \nabla_i^- f\left(\*n\right) = \+L f\left(\*n\right),
    \]
    where \(\+L\) is the linear-death generator in \eqref{eq:birth-death-generator}.
    \label{prop:point-process-lift}
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
Under \(\Pi_{\bar\nu}\), the marked counts are independent with law \(\-{Pois}\left(1 / d\right)\), and, conditional on these counts, the point locations in each fiber are independent with law \(\nu\). Hence
    \[
    \Pi_{\bar\nu}\left(\*N = \*n\right) = e^{-1} \frac{d^{-\left\|\*n\right\|_1}}{\*n!}.
    \]
    Comparing this mass with \(\mu\left(\*n\right)\) proves \eqref{eq:point-process-lift-density}. The Papangelou intensity is the add-one ratio of this density, which gives \eqref{eq:point-process-lift-papangelou}.

    If \(F = f \circ \*N\), then \(\nabla_{\left(x, i\right)}^+ F\left(\eta\right) = \nabla_i^+ f\left(\*n\right)\), independently of \(x\). Similarly, removing any point in the \(i\)-th fiber produces \(\nabla_i^- f\left(\*n\right)\). Since \(\bar\nu\left(X \times \left\{i\right\}\right) = 1 / d\), substituting \eqref{eq:point-process-lift-papangelou} into \eqref{eq:point-process-glauber-generator} yields the claimed generator identity.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- theorem-28: body_md -->
Suppose that the infimum in \eqref{eq:static-schrodinger-bridge} is finite and attained. Then there are nonnegative functions \(f_0, g_1: \Omega \to \mathbb R_{\ge 0}\) such that
    \[
    \frac{\,\-d P^{\star}}{\,\-d R}\left(\*p_{\left[0, 1\right]}\right) = f_0\left(\*p_0\right) g_1\left(\*p_1\right).
    \]
    Define
    \[
    f_t\left(\*z\right) := \*E_{\*p_{\left[0, 1\right]} \sim R}\left[f_0\left(\*p_0\right) \mid \*p_t = \*z\right], \qquad g_t\left(\*z\right) := \*E_{\*p_{\left[0, 1\right]} \sim R}\left[g_1\left(\*p_1\right) \mid \*p_t = \*z\right].
    \]
    Then \(P^{\star}\) is Markov, its time-\(t\) marginal satisfies
    \[
    \frac{\,\-d P_t^{\star}}{\,\-d R_t}\left(\*p_t\right) = f_t\left(\*p_t\right) g_t\left(\*p_t\right),
    \]
    and, for \(0 \le s \le t \le 1\), its forward and backward transition kernels are
    \[
    P_{s \to t}^{\star}\left(\*p_s, \*p_t\right) = \frac{g_t\left(\*p_t\right)}{g_s\left(\*p_s\right)} R_{s \to t}\left(\*p_s, \*p_t\right), \qquad P_{t \to s}^{\star}\left(\*p_t, \*p_s\right) = \frac{f_s\left(\*p_s\right)}{f_t\left(\*p_t\right)} R_{t \to s}\left(\*p_t, \*p_s\right).
    \]
    If \(\+L_t^R\) and \(\Gamma_t^R\) are the generator and carr\'e du champ of the reference process, then
    \begin{equation}
        \+L_t^{P^{\star}} u = \+L_t^R u + \frac{2 \Gamma_t^R\left(g_t, u\right)}{g_t}.
        \label{eq:schrodinger-bridge-doob-transform}
    \end{equation}
    \label{thm:markovian-schrodinger-bridge}
<!-- end theorem-28 -->
<!-- theorem-29: body_md -->
Let \(\left(\nu_t\right)\) denote the linear-tilt localization scheme defined by
    \[
    \,\-d \nu_t\left(\*n\right) = \nu_t\left(\*n\right) \left\langle\*n - \!{mean}\left(\nu_t\right),\,\,\-d \*Z_t\right\rangle,
    \]
    where \(\left(\*Z_t\right)\) is a martingale satisfying
    \[
    \*E\left[\,\-d \*Z_t \mid \+F_t\right] = 0.
    \]
    Then the SDE for \(\left(\!{cov}\left(\nu_t\right)\right)\) is
    \[
    \,\-d \, \!{cov}\left(\nu_t\right) = -\!{cov}\left(\nu_t\right) \,\-d \left\langle\*Z\right\rangle_t  \!{cov}\left(\nu_t\right) + \,\-d \, \-{Martingale}_t.
    \]
    \label{thm:trickle-down-equation}
<!-- end theorem-29 -->
<!-- corollary-9: body_md -->
Let \(\mu\) be a probability measure on \(\mathbb N^d\) with downward closed support. Let \(\left(\nu_t\right)_{t \in \left[0, 1\right]}\) denote the corresponding localization process given by Poisson stochastic localization. Define \(\rho_t^{\*x}\) as in \Cref{lem:tilted-pinning-conditional-law}:
    \[
    \rho_t^{\*x} := \-{Law}\left(\*X_1 - \*X_t \mid \*X_t = \*x\right) = \left(1 - t\right) * \mu^{\*x}, \quad t \in \left(0, 1\right), \, \*x \in \operatorname{supp}\left(\mu\right).
    \]
    Then the SDE for \(\left(\rho_t^{\*X_t}\right)_{t \in \left(0, 1\right)}\) is
    \[
    \,\-d \, \!{cov}\left(\rho_t^{\*X_t}\right) = -\frac{1}{1 - t} \!{cov}\left(\rho_t^{\*X_t}\right) \operatorname{diag}\left(\!{mean}\left(\rho_t^{\*X_t}\right)\right)^{\dagger} \!{cov}\left(\rho_t^{\*X_t}\right) \,\-d t + \,\-d \, \-{Martingale}_t, \quad t \in \left(0, 1\right).
    \]
    \label{cor:trickle-down-tilted-pinning}
<!-- end corollary-9 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
Translation by \(\*X_t\) does not change covariance, so
    \[
    \!{cov}\left(\rho_t^{\*X_t}\right) = \!{cov}\left(\nu_t\right).
    \]
    Write \(\*a_t := \!{mean}\left(\nu_t\right) - \*X_t = \!{mean}\left(\rho_t^{\*X_t}\right)\). By \Cref{thm:poisson-linear-tilt}, the driving martingale satisfies \(\,\-d Z_{t, i} = \,\-d M_{t, i} / a_{t-, i}\) on the coordinates for which \(a_{t-, i} > 0\). The coordinate counting processes have no simultaneous jumps, and hence
    \[
    \,\-d \left\langle\*M\right\rangle_t = \operatorname{diag}\left(\*q_t\left(\*X_{t-}\right)\right) \,\-d t.
    \]
    By \Cref{cor:denoising-birth-rates-conditional-expectation}, \(\*q_t\left(\*X_{t-}\right) = \*a_{t-} / \left(1 - t\right)\). Therefore,
    \[
    \,\-d \left\langle\*Z\right\rangle_t = \frac{1}{1 - t} \operatorname{diag}\left(\*a_{t-}\right)^{-1} \,\-d t,
    \]
    where the inverse is taken on the coordinates on which \(a_{t-, i} > 0\), and both sides vanish on the remaining coordinates. Substituting this bracket into \Cref{thm:trickle-down-equation} gives the claimed SDE.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
For every \(\*x \in \operatorname{supp}\left(\mu\right)\), the function \(\eta_{\*x}\) is locally Lipschitz on \(\left(0, 1\right)\). If \(\mu\) is finitely supported, then \(\eta\) is also locally Lipschitz on \(\left(0, 1\right)\).
    \label{lem:regularity-of-eta}
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
Fix \(\*x \in \operatorname{supp}\left(\mu\right)\), and let \(\+I_{\*x} := \left\{i \in \left[d\right] \,:\, \*x + \*e_i \in \operatorname{supp}\left(\mu\right)\right\}\). Downward closure implies that the coordinates outside \(\+I_{\*x}\) vanish under \(\rho_t^{\*x}\). On \(\+I_{\*x}\), set
    \[
    \*C_{\*x}\left(t\right) := \!{cov}\left(\rho_t^{\*x}\right), \qquad \*D_{\*x}\left(t\right) := \operatorname{diag}\left(\!{mean}\left(\rho_t^{\*x}\right)\right), \qquad \*A_{\*x}\left(t\right) := \*D_{\*x}\left(t\right)^{-1/2} \*C_{\*x}\left(t\right) \*D_{\*x}\left(t\right)^{-1/2}.
    \]
    Every diagonal entry of \(\*D_{\*x}\left(t\right)\) is positive on \(\+I_{\*x}\). Writing \(a\left(\*n\right) := \*n! \mu\left(\*n\right)\), the law \(\rho_t^{\*x}\) has mass function proportional to
    \[
    \frac{a\left(\*x + \*k\right)}{\*k!} \left(1 - t\right)^{\left\|\*k\right\|_1}.
    \]
    Its moments are therefore analytic in \(t\) on \(\left(0, 1\right)\). It follows that \(\*A_{\*x}\) is analytic there. Since
    \[
    \eta_{\*x}\left(t\right) = \lambda_{\max}\left(\*A_{\*x}\left(t\right)\right),
    \]
    the standard eigenvalue perturbation bound shows that \(\eta_{\*x}\) is locally Lipschitz. If \(\+I_{\*x} = \varnothing\), then \(\eta_{\*x} \equiv 0\), so the same conclusion holds. When \(\mu\) has finite support, \(\eta\) is the maximum of finitely many locally Lipschitz functions and is therefore locally Lipschitz.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
For every \(\*x \in \operatorname{supp}\left(\mu\right)\) with \(\+I_{\*x} \ne \varnothing\),
    \[
    \eta_{\*x}\left(1^-\right) = 1.
    \]
    If \(\+I_{\*x} = \varnothing\), then \(\eta_{\*x} \equiv 0\). Moreover, if the \(\delta\)-ULC condition \eqref{eq:ulc-condition} holds at \(\*n = \*x\), then
    \[
    \eta_{\*x}\left(1 - \varepsilon\right) \le 1 + \left(1 - \delta\right) \varepsilon + O\left(\varepsilon^2\right) \quad \text{as } \varepsilon \to 0^+.
    \]
    In particular, if \(\mu\) is finitely supported and \(\delta\)-ULC, then
    \[
    \eta\left(1 - \varepsilon\right) \le 1 + \left(1 - \delta\right) \varepsilon + O\left(\varepsilon^2\right) \quad \text{as } \varepsilon \to 0^+.
    \]
    If, in addition, \(\mu \ne \delta_{\*0}\), then \(\eta\left(1^-\right) = 1\); for \(\mu = \delta_{\*0}\), one has \(\eta \equiv 0\).
    \label{lem:eta-t-approaches-1}
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
Fix \(\*x\) with \(\+I_{\*x} \ne \varnothing\), write \(a\left(\*n\right) := \*n! \mu\left(\*n\right)\), and set
    \[
    r_i := \frac{a\left(\*x + \*e_i\right)}{a\left(\*x\right)}, \qquad \*R_{\*x} := \operatorname{diag}\left(r_i\right)_{i \in \+I_{\*x}}, \qquad \*K_{\*x} := \left(1 - \frac{a\left(\*x\right) a\left(\*x + \*e_i + \*e_j\right)}{a\left(\*x + \*e_i\right) a\left(\*x + \*e_j\right)}\right)_{i, j \in \+I_{\*x}}.
    \]
    Let
    \[
    h_{\*x}\left(\boldsymbol{\theta}\right) := \sum_{\*k \in \mathbb N^d} \frac{a\left(\*x + \*k\right)}{\*k!} \boldsymbol{\theta}^{\*k}.
    \]
    As in \eqref{eq:tilted-pinning-log-hessian}, with \(\boldsymbol{\theta} = \varepsilon \*1\),
    \[
    \!{cov}\left(\rho_{1 - \varepsilon}^{\*x}\right) = \operatorname{diag}\left(\!{mean}\left(\rho_{1 - \varepsilon}^{\*x}\right)\right) + \varepsilon^2 \nabla^2 \log h_{\*x}\left(\varepsilon \*1\right).
    \]
    Moreover,
    \[
    \!{mean}\left(\rho_{1 - \varepsilon}^{\*x}\right) = \varepsilon \left(r_i\right)_{i \in \+I_{\*x}} + O\left(\varepsilon^2\right), \qquad \nabla^2 \log h_{\*x}\left(\varepsilon \*1\right) = \left(\frac{a\left(\*x + \*e_i + \*e_j\right)}{a\left(\*x\right)} - r_i r_j\right)_{i, j \in \+I_{\*x}} + O\left(\varepsilon\right).
    \]
    Consequently, the normalized covariance from the proof of \Cref{lem:regularity-of-eta} satisfies
    \[
    \*A_{\*x}\left(1 - \varepsilon\right) = \*I - \varepsilon \*R_{\*x}^{1 / 2} \*K_{\*x} \*R_{\*x}^{1 / 2} + O\left(\varepsilon^2\right).
    \]
    This already gives \(\eta_{\*x}\left(1^-\right) = 1\). If the \(\delta\)-ULC condition holds at \(\*x\), then
    \[
    \*K_{\*x} + \left(1 - \delta\right) \*R_{\*x}^{-1} \succeq \*O,
    \]
    and hence
    \[
    -\*R_{\*x}^{1 / 2} \*K_{\*x} \*R_{\*x}^{1 / 2} \preceq \left(1 - \delta\right) \*I.
    \]
    Taking the largest eigenvalue in the preceding expansion proves
    \[
    \eta_{\*x}\left(1 - \varepsilon\right) \le 1 + \left(1 - \delta\right) \varepsilon + O\left(\varepsilon^2\right).
    \]
    If \(\mu\) is finitely supported, the support contains only finitely many \(\*x\), so the error term is uniform in \(\*x\). Taking the maximum proves the final assertions.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
Suppose that \(\mu\) is finitely supported. Then, for every \(t \in \left(0, 1\right)\),
    \[
    \eta\left(t\right) \le \eta\left(t + \varepsilon\right) + \frac{\eta\left(t\right)^2 - \eta\left(t\right)}{1 - t} \varepsilon + O\left(\varepsilon^2\right) \quad \text{as } \varepsilon \to 0^+.
    \]
    \label{lem:eta-t-0-to-1}
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
Along the localization process, write
    \[
    \*C_s := \!{cov}\left(\rho_s^{\*X_s}\right), \qquad \*D_s := \operatorname{diag}\left(\!{mean}\left(\rho_s^{\*X_s}\right)\right).
    \]
    All inverses below are generalized inverses, or equivalently inverses restricted to the coordinates on which the corresponding mean is positive. Integrating \Cref{cor:trickle-down-tilted-pinning} from \(t\) to \(t + \varepsilon\) and conditioning on \(\+F_t\) gives
    \[
    \*C_t = \*E\left[\*C_{t + \varepsilon} \mid \+F_t\right] + \*E\left[\int_t^{t + \varepsilon} \frac{1}{1 - s} \*C_s \*D_s^{\dagger} \*C_s \,\-d s \mathrel{\big|} \+F_t\right].
    \]
    By the definition of \(\eta\),
    \[
    \*C_s \preceq \eta\left(s\right) \*D_s, \qquad \*C_s \*D_s^{\dagger} \*C_s \preceq \eta\left(s\right)^2 \*D_s.
    \]
    Hence,
    \[
    \*C_t \preceq \eta\left(t + \varepsilon\right) \*E\left[\*D_{t + \varepsilon} \mid \+F_t\right] + \*E\left[\int_t^{t + \varepsilon} \frac{\eta\left(s\right)^2}{1 - s} \*D_s \,\-d s \mathrel{\big|} \+F_t\right].
    \]
    Set \(\*a_s := \!{mean}\left(\rho_s^{\*X_s}\right)\). The tower property and the martingale property of the denoising birth rates yield, for \(s \ge t\),
    \[
    \*E\left[\*a_s \mid \+F_t\right] = \*a_t - \*E\left[\*X_s - \*X_t \mid \+F_t\right] = \*a_t - \int_t^s \*E\left[\*q_u\left(\*X_u\right) \mid \+F_t\right] \,\-d u = \left(1 - \frac{s - t}{1 - t}\right) \*a_t.
    \]
    Therefore,
    \[
    \*E\left[\*D_s \mid \+F_t\right] = \frac{1 - s}{1 - t} \*D_t.
    \]
    Substituting this estimate into the preceding inequality gives
    \[
    \*C_t \preceq \left(\left(1 - \frac{\varepsilon}{1 - t}\right) \eta\left(t + \varepsilon\right) + \frac{1}{1 - t} \int_t^{t + \varepsilon} \eta\left(s\right)^2 \,\-d s\right) \*D_t.
    \]
    Taking the maximum over the finitely many possible values of \(\*X_t\) yields
    \[
    \eta\left(t\right) \le \left(1 - \frac{\varepsilon}{1 - t}\right) \eta\left(t + \varepsilon\right) + \frac{1}{1 - t} \int_t^{t + \varepsilon} \eta\left(s\right)^2 \,\-d s.
    \]
    By \Cref{lem:regularity-of-eta}, \(\eta\) is locally Lipschitz, so
    \[
    \int_t^{t + \varepsilon} \eta\left(s\right)^2 \,\-d s = \eta\left(t\right)^2 \varepsilon + O\left(\varepsilon^2\right), \qquad \eta\left(t + \varepsilon\right) = \eta\left(t\right) + O\left(\varepsilon\right).
    \]
    It follows that
    \[
    \eta\left(t\right) \le \eta\left(t + \varepsilon\right) + \frac{\eta\left(t\right)^2 - \eta\left(t\right)}{1 - t} \varepsilon + O\left(\varepsilon^2\right) \quad \text{as } \varepsilon \to 0^+,
    \]
    as claimed.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- theorem-30: body_md -->
Let \(\mu\) be a \(\delta\)-ULC probability measure on \(\mathbb N^d\). Then, for \(t \in \left(0, 1\right)\), \(\left(1 - t\right) * \mu^{\*x}\) is \(1 / \left(1 - \left(1 - \delta\right) \left(1 - t\right)\right)\)-spectrally independent for every \(\*x \in \operatorname{supp}\left(\mu\right)\). Moreover, \(\mu\) satisfies the weighted Poincar\'e\xspace inequality with constant \(\delta\):
    \[
    \delta \, \*{Var}_{\mu}\left[f\right] \le \*E_{\mu}\left[\sum_{i = 1}^d \frac{\left(n_i + 1\right) \mu\left(\*n + \*e_i\right)}{\mu\left(\*n\right)} \left(\nabla_i^+ f\left(\*n\right)\right)^2\right], \quad \forall f \in \+D\left(\+E\right).
    \]
    Equivalently, the birth-death generator \(\+L\) defined in \eqref{eq:birth-death-generator} has spectral gap at least \(\delta\).
    \label{thm:ulc-poincare-trickle-down}
<!-- end theorem-30 -->
<!-- remark-17: body_md -->
The \(\delta\)-ULC matrix appears here as the terminal boundary condition for the normalized covariance flow. Thus the trickle-down argument does more than recover the weighted Poincar\'e\xspace inequality: it identifies \(\delta\)-ULC as precisely the local second-order condition that initiates the trickle-down analysis along Poisson stochastic localization.
<!-- end remark-17 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
We first assume that \(\mu\) has finite support. If \(\mu = \delta_{\*0}\), both conclusions are immediate, so suppose otherwise. By \Cref{lem:regularity-of-eta}, \Cref{lem:eta-t-approaches-1}, and \Cref{lem:eta-t-0-to-1}, we have
    \begin{equation}
        \eta\left(t\right) \le \frac{1}{1 - \left(1 - \delta\right) \left(1 - t\right)}.
        \label{eq:eta-trickle-down-bound}
    \end{equation}
    Hence, for \(t \in \left(0, 1\right)\), \(\left(1 - t\right) * \mu^{\*x}\) is \(1 / \left(1 - \left(1 - \delta\right) \left(1 - t\right)\right)\)-spectrally independent for every \(\*x \in \operatorname{supp}\left(\mu\right)\). By \Cref{prop:sufficient-condition-approximate-conservation},
    \[
    \partial_t \*E\left[\*{Var}_{\nu_t}\left[f\right]\right] \ge -\frac{\*E\left[\*{Var}_{\nu_t}\left[f\right]\right]}{\left(1 - t\right) \left(1 - \left(1 - \delta\right) \left(1 - t\right)\right)}, \quad \forall t \in \left(0, 1\right).
    \]
    It follows that
    \[
    \gamma_t = \inf_{\substack{f \in \+C_{\-c}\left(\operatorname{supp}\left(\mu\right)\right) \\ \*{Var}_{\mu}\left[f\right] > 0}} \frac{\*E\left[\*{Var}_{\nu_t}\left[f\right]\right]}{\*{Var}_{\mu}\left[f\right]} \ge \exp\left(-\int_0^t \frac{1}{\left(1 - s\right) \left(1 - \left(1 - \delta\right) \left(1 - s\right)\right)} \,\-d s\right) = \frac{\delta \left(1 - t\right)}{t + \delta \left(1 - t\right)}.
    \]
    Consequently,
    \[
    \liminf_{\varepsilon \to 0^+} \frac{\gamma_{1 - \varepsilon}}{\varepsilon} \ge \delta,
    \]
    and \Cref{thm:limiting-process-functional-inequalities} proves the weighted Poincar\'e\xspace inequality with constant \(\delta\) for finitely supported \(\delta\)-ULC \(\mu\).

    We now remove the finite-support assumption. For \(N \in \mathbb N\), apply the coordinate-box restrictions \(S_N\) and conditional measures \(\mu_N\) introduced in the proof of \Cref{thm:ulc-poincare-inequality}. For every fixed \(t \in \left(0, 1\right)\) and \(\*x \in \operatorname{supp}\left(\mu\right)\), the tilted pinnings \(\left(1 - t\right) * \mu_N^{\*x}\) converge to \(\left(1 - t\right) * \mu^{\*x}\) together with their first two moments. Thus, the finite-support covariance bounds pass to the limit and prove the first conclusion. The finite-support result applied to \(\mu_N\) also gives
    \[
    \delta \, \*{Var}_{\mu_N}\left[f\right] \le \+E_N\left(f, f\right).
    \]
    For every \(f \in \+D\left(\+E\right)\), one has \(\*{Var}_{\mu_N}\left[f\right] \to \*{Var}_{\mu}\left[f\right]\) and \(\+E_N\left(f, f\right) \to \+E\left(f, f\right)\) as \(N \to \infty\). Passing to the limit proves the claimed weighted Poincar\'e\xspace inequality on \(\+D\left(\+E\right)\).
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- proposition-8: body_md -->
Let \(\mu\) be a probability measure supported on \(\mathbb N^d\) with downward closed support.
